title.narrative: UNICEF: Scaling Up Nutrition (SUN ) Phase II
UNICEF: Scaling Up Nutrition (SUN) Phase II

description.narrative:
The main objective of the intervention is to reduce stunting of children under two by 7% in the 17 districts under SUN II, with the following expected outcomes;
Outcome 1: Sustained practice of optimal nutrition behaviours amongst adolescents, pregnant women, mothers and caregivers of children under two
Outcome 2: Sustained demand for and use of agriculture, health and WASH interventions for adolescents, pregnant women, mothers and caregivers of children under two and communities
Outcome 3: Quality nutrition information is used by communities, government and partners for evidence-based decisions, action and advocacy
Outcome 4: Sustained commitment by government and partners for accountable nutrition governance.

UNICEF has applied to donors, Sweden, UK, Germany and the European Union for funding of USD 50.1MUSD to support the implementation of the scaling Up Nutrition Phase II Project. (SUN Phase II) The SUN Phase II will support delivery of high-impact priority nutrition specific and sensitive interventions for the reduction of chronic malnutrition (stunting) in children less than 2 years in the 17 targeted intervention districts in Zambia (Chipata, Chongwe, Lundazi, Chienge, Chinsali, Isoka, Mpika, Lusaka, Mwinilunga, Solwezi, Zambezi, Choma, Monze, Kalabo, Kaoma, Mongu and Shangombo districts), during the period 2019-2023. The overall objective is to "to reduce stunting of children aged below 2 years at a rate of 2 percentage points per year in all target 17 districts." Meaning that the percentage of stunted children below 2 years will reduce from 29% in 2019 to 21% in 2023 and this is measured by programme specific baseline and endline evaluations. The expected outcomes for the programme are; Outcome 1: Sustained practice of optimal nutrition behaviours amongst adolescents, pregnant women, mothers and caregivers of children under two; Outcome 2: Sustained demand for and use of agriculture, health and WASH interventions for adolescents, pregnant women, mothers and caregivers of children under two and communities; Outcome 3: Quality nutrition information is used by communities, government and partners for evidence-based decisions, action and advocacy; Outcome 4: Sustained commitment by government and partners for accountable nutrition governance. UNICEF will sub-contract 3 implementing NGOs to provide required technical assistance to districts and communities. At national level UNICEF will support the National Food and Nutrition Commission and key government Ministries.
UNICEF will also draw upon expertise from other UN agencies providing technical assistance for nutrition-sensitive interventions, namely, the World Health Organisation (WHO), the World Food Programme (WFP) and the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO). Due to the preference of the other donors supporting the project, it has been decided that the project support modality through UNICEF will be used to support the programme rather than a joint UN programme. UNICEF will be responsible for coordinating technical assistance from other UN agencies in alignment with identified needs. UNICEF will establish UN-to-UN agreements and transfer funds for national-level costs through direct transfer from UNICEF to the other UN agency. The roles and responsibilities of each participating agency have been agreed and are clearly spelled out in the proposal.
The intervention’s total budget is 50.1 million USD, out of which Sweden will contribute 95MSEK. The remaining amount will be provided by UK (15M Pounds), Germany (10-12M Euro) and the European Union (10M Euro).

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution UNICEF SUN II

description.narrative:
As the SUN-II program nears its conclusion (activity period ending 30 April 2025), recent efforts have focused on accelerating progress towards set targets, reflecting on successes and challenges, sustaining long-term investments, and facilitating closeout activities in five districts not affected by drought. The challenges from the 2023/2024 drought have persisted and implementation of targeted drought response activities through repurposed funds has advanced in drought affected districts.
Results achieved
The program advanced with its strategic approach to inform future nutrition initiatives, ensuring that lessons learned are incorporated into ongoing and new programs. This approach leverages community health platforms to maximize impact for nutrition outcomes and strengthens public financial management to secure sustained nutrition funding. Additionally, the program in collaboration with cooperating partners has advocated for the increased use of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) to support targeted nutrition interventions and reinforce key nutrition priorities within the Office of the Vice President. Collaborative engagement has also been maintained and strengthened with other nutrition programs, such as the World Banks Girls' Education and Women's Empowerment and Livelihoods (GEWEL II) initiative, which Sweden is also supporting.
During the period from June to November 2024, the SUN II program achieved significant results across its key areas including the key results below:
Nutrition and Health: The program improved optimal nutrition behaviours among adolescents, pregnant women, and caregivers of children under 2. It reached 1,542,768 households with nutrition counselling and directly engaged 307,249 households through 26,104 trained volunteers. The program also supported Child Health Week, reaching 947,369 children with Vitamin A supplementation and 844,973 with deworming. Additionally, 1,096,591 children were screened for malnutrition, with 2,616 treated for severe acute malnutrition and 7,673 for moderate acute malnutrition.
Agriculture and Food Security: Access to diversified and nutritious food improved, with 154,424 households trained in nutrient-dense crop production. The program distributed goats and chickens to households, enhancing dietary diversification. A total of 90,706 households received nutrient-rich inputs, and 2,911 households received animal inputs. Training in the utilization of Non-Wood Forest Products reached 16,097 households.
Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH): The program rehabilitated 192 boreholes, providing safe water to 57,885 people. It also improved sanitation and handwashing facilities, benefiting 8,576 and 4,906 people respectively. The cumulative beneficiaries for sanitation and handwashing facilities reached 665,092 and 556,541 people.
Social Protection and Economic Empowerment: The program referred 3,459 households to social protection services and supported 18,489 households in joining Village Savings and Lending Associations (VSLAs). It also facilitated the formation of 21 new Savings and Credit Cooperative Organizations (SACCOs) and linked VSLA members to financial institutions.
Last five months of implementation
In the final five months of the SUN II program (January - April 2025), the focus will be on accelerating drought-response efforts using repurposed funds to save lives and safeguard livelihoods, while also conducting key closeout activities such as final reporting, archiving documents, compliance reviews, completing planned activities, managing asset disposition, and engaging stakeholders to ensure a structured and accountable conclusion, with all parties informed about the program's achievements and legacy.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
